descriptor: Design system for Jira, Confluence & Atlassian apps

sections.overview:
### Overview
> Source: https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md ; https://atlassian.design/tokens/design-tokens

Atlassian Design System (ADS) is the product design system behind Jira, Confluence, Trello, and other Atlassian apps. It is token-first: color, space, typography, elevation, and shape are expressed as semantic design tokens (`@atlaskit/tokens`) rather than raw values, so light and dark themes resolve from a single set of token names.

### Character
- Neutral-dominant canvas with restrained saturation — color carries meaning, depth is earned, not decorative.
- Built on an 8px spacing rhythm, a t-shirt radius scale, and a four-plane elevation model.
- Two themes ship today: light and dark. High-contrast, and non-color themes (density, reduced motion, custom typography) are described as future directions.
- Self-described reference points: aligned with IBM Carbon (token discipline), Linear (restraint), GitHub Primer (neutral backbone + semantic accents); explicitly not Material (heavier elevation/saturation) or Tailwind/Shadcn defaults.

### Distribution
- Docs at atlassian.design; React component library `@atlaskit/*`.
- Agent-facing delivery: a topic-split `llms.txt`, a portable `DESIGN.md` manifest (rules stated with RFC 2119 MUST/SHOULD), an ADS MCP server, an `atlassian-design-system` skill, and ESLint/Stylelint plugins.

### Not published
- ADS abstracts most raw hex behind tokens. Hex values shown in `DESIGN.md` are labeled "this build's theme" and may change; a separate color-palettes page holds hex/RGBA and is partly access-gated.
sections.colors:
### Colors
> Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/color-new ; https://atlassian.design/tokens/design-tokens ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

Color is applied through semantic design tokens, never hardcoded hex. Token names read foundation → property → modifier, e.g. `color.text`, `color.background.accent.blue.subtle`, `color.icon.success`. ADS deliberately abstracts hex behind tokens so themes can remap values — prefer token names over raw values.

### Four color types (not interchangeable)
- **Neutrals & surfaces** — backbone for ~80–90% of the canvas.
- **Semantic roles** — carry meaning (see role table).
- **Accent ramps** — decoration only (tags, file types, avatars). Ten hues: gray, red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, magenta, lime — each on lightness steps subtlest → subtler → subtle → bolder.
- **Chart colors** — data visualization only (see Data Visualization).

### Color roles
| Role | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `neutral` | Default text, secondary UI (secondary buttons, nav). |
| `brand` | Primary actions / Atlassian brand elements. |
| `information` | Informative UI, in-progress. |
| `success` | Favorable outcome / success messages. |
| `warning` | Caution to prevent a mistake. |
| `danger` | Danger / serious error states. |
| `discovery` | New / onboarding / feature info. |
| `accent` | Colors with no semantic meaning (interchangeable). |
| `inverse` | UI on bold-emphasis backgrounds. |
| `input` | Form fields. |

### Neutral & surface tokens
Hex below is quoted from `DESIGN.md` and reflects that build's light theme; ADS flags these as theme-resolved, not a canonical palette.

| Token | Hex (build theme) | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | Page / card fill |
| `surface.sunken` | `#F8F8F8` | Wells, columns, grouped panels inside a page |
| `surface.raised` | `#FFFFFF` | Movable card (pair with `shadow.raised`) |
| `surface.overlay` | `#FFFFFF` | Modal / popover / toast shell (pair with `shadow.overlay`) |
| `color.text` | `#292A2E` | Paragraph copy |
| `color.text.subtle` | `#505258` | Labels, metadata |
| `color.text.subtlest` | `#6B6E76` | Placeholders, hints |
| `color.border` | `#0B120E24` (alpha) | Hairline dividers |
| `color.border.bold` | `#7D818A` | Stronger divider |
| `color.border.input` | `#8C8F97` | Field outline |
| `color.border.focused` | `#4688EC` | 2px focus ring color |
| `color.link` / `.pressed` | `#1868DB` / `#1558BC` | Text links |

### Emphasis & interaction states
- Emphasis runs subtlest → boldest (contrast against the default surface). `inverse` text/border/icon tokens sit on bold backgrounds; bold warning backgrounds (yellow) use special `warning.inverse` tokens to pass AA.
- Interaction-state tokens: hovered, pressed, selected, focused, disabled. There are no dedicated hovered/pressed icon tokens — use a subtle neutral background instead.

### Known gaps
- Raw hex/RGBA and light→dark mappings are pushed to a separate "color palettes" page (partly access-gated); the color foundation itself lists no hex.
- Hex quoted here is theme-resolved from `DESIGN.md`, not an authoritative fixed palette.
sections.typography:
### Typography
> Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/typography-beta ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

App typeface is **Atlassian Sans** (body + headings) with **Atlassian Mono** for code; **Charlie Sans/Display** is reserved for brand/marketing, never product chrome. Type is tokenized (`font.heading.*`, `font.body*`, `font.metric.*`, `font.code`) and consumed via the Heading / Text components rather than raw CSS. Tokens use **rem** (1rem = 16px browser default) for accessibility/zoom.

### Heading scale
| Token | Weight | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `font.heading.xxlarge` | Bold | 2rem / 32px | 2.25rem / 36px |
| `font.heading.xlarge` | Bold | 1.75rem / 28px | 2rem / 32px |
| `font.heading.large` | Bold | 1.5rem / 24px | 1.75rem / 28px |
| `font.heading.medium` | Bold | 1.25rem / 20px | 1.5rem / 24px |
| `font.heading.small` | Bold | 1rem / 16px | 1.25rem / 20px |
| `font.heading.xsmall` | Bold | 0.875rem / 14px | 1.25rem / 20px |
| `font.heading.xxsmall` | Bold | 0.75rem / 12px | 1rem / 16px |

### Body scale
| Token | Weight | Size | Line height | Paragraph spacing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `font.body.large` | Regular | 1rem / 16px | 1.5rem / 24px | 1rem / 16px |
| `font.body` (default) | Regular | 0.875rem / 14px | 1.25rem / 20px | 0.75rem / 12px |
| `font.body.small` | Regular | 0.75rem / 12px | 1rem / 16px | 0.5rem / 8px |

### Metric scale
| Token | Weight | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `font.metric.large` | Bold | 1.75rem / 28px | 2rem / 32px |
| `font.metric.medium` | Bold | 1.5rem / 24px | 1.75rem / 28px |
| `font.metric.small` | Bold | 1rem / 16px | 1.25rem / 20px |

### Code
- **Code block** (`font.code`): Regular, 12px / 20px line height. Inline code is relative to its container (≈12.25px inside a 14px body).

### Weights & case
- Weight tokens: `weight-regular` (body), `weight-medium` (text beside icons), `weight-bold` (rare emphasis).
- **Sentence case for every user-visible string** — titles, headings, buttons, labels, tabs, tooltips, table headers. Title Case and ALL CAPS / letter-spaced eyebrows are drift patterns.

### Not published
- Typography is in **beta** (refreshed system rolling out). Exact numeric font-weight values are not published — set weight via tokens.
sections.layout:
### Layout
> Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/spacing ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

Spacing is an **8px base-unit** system; the base unit is the token `space.100` (8px), and every step is a multiple. The numeric suffix is the percentage of the base unit (e.g. `space.200` = 200% = 16px). Every gap, padding, margin, and inset must land on a token step — no off-grid values. Layout is built from primitives (Box, Stack, Inline, Flex, Grid, Bleed), not raw CSS.

### Space scale
| Token | Multiplier | rem | px |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `space.0` | 0× | 0 | 0px |
| `space.025` | 0.25× | 0.125rem | 2px |
| `space.050` | 0.5× | 0.25rem | 4px |
| `space.075` | 0.75× | 0.375rem | 6px |
| `space.100` | 1× | 0.5rem | 8px |
| `space.150` | 1.5× | 0.75rem | 12px |
| `space.200` | 2× | 1rem | 16px |
| `space.250` | 2.5× | 1.25rem | 20px |
| `space.300` | 3× | 1.5rem | 24px |
| `space.400` | 4× | 2rem | 32px |
| `space.500` | 5× | 2.5rem | 40px |
| `space.600` | 6× | 3rem | 48px |
| `space.800` | 8× | 4rem | 64px |
| `space.1000` | 10× | 5rem | 80px |

### Usage ranges & principles
- Negative space tokens run `space.negative.025` → `space.negative.400` (-2px to -32px), for bleed/overlap; prefer the Bleed primitive first.
- Small (0–8px): icon/text gaps, badge/icon-button/table-cell padding, input padding. Medium (12–24px): larger component padding, card spacing. Large (32–80px): page-level layout.
- Compose relationships by proximity, use consistent spacing in repeating elements, vary the step to express hierarchy; optical adjustments of ±1 step allowed, starting from a token.
- Multi-column pages (per `DESIGN.md`): 12-column grid, `space.300` gutters, `space.400` page padding.

### Not published
- ADS doesn't publish fixed breakpoint pixel tokens in the spacing/layout foundation. `DESIGN.md` names 320 / 768 / 1280px as reference breakpoints (guidance, not tokens).
sections.depth:
### Elevation & Depth
> Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/elevation ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

Elevation is a **four-plane** system plus an overflow treatment. Each plane pairs a surface token with (for the top two) a matching shadow token; raising or overlaying is an intentional choice. Elevation surfaces use neutral palettes and are all applied via tokens — shadow values are never hand-authored.

### The planes
| Plane | Surface token | Shadow token | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sunken | `elevation.surface.sunken` | — | Wells/backdrops that group content (Kanban columns). Only on the default surface. |
| Default | `elevation.surface` | — | Flat baseline canvas (e.g. a Confluence page); flat cards use a border. |
| Raised | `elevation.surface.raised` | `elevation.shadow.raised` | Movable cards (Jira/Trello). At most one raised region per screen. |
| Overlay | `elevation.surface.overlay` | `elevation.shadow.overlay` | Modals, dialogs, dropdowns, floating toolbars, flags, popovers, tooltips. Can stack. |

### Rules
- Always pair raised↔`shadow.raised` and overlay↔`shadow.overlay`; mixing shadows across planes is a bug. Especially important in dark mode, where higher surfaces get lighter (shadows are harder to see).
- Hovered/pressed states change surface color (`.hovered` / `.pressed` tokens); optionally transition planes on hover/press, but never combine both techniques.
- For scrolled content, a **border at the clip edge is the default cue**; use `elevation.shadow.overflow` (with `.spread` + `.perimeter` fallbacks) only where a border would be missed (horizontal table scroll, modal body).
- `elevation.surface.sunken` (opaque, darkens in both modes) differs from `color.background.neutral` (transparent, adapts to elevation).

### Z-index
| Z-index | Example | Elevation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | — | None |
| 200 | Atlassian navigation | Default |
| 300 | Inline dialog | Overlay |
| 400 | Popup | Overlay |
| 500 | Blanket | None |
| 510 | Modal | Overlay |
| 600 | Flag | Overlay |
| 700 | Spotlight | Overlay |
| 800 | Tooltip | None |

### Not published
- Numeric shadow offset/blur/spread values are not published in the elevation foundation — they live in the token reference and are consumed as tokens.
sections.shapes:
### Shapes
> Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/border ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

Corner radius follows a **t-shirt scale**, and each size maps to a component class — pick radius by what the thing is, not by taste. Border widths sit on a separate three-step scale where stroke weight carries meaning (resting vs selected vs focused).

### Corner radius scale
Values below are quoted from `DESIGN.md`.

| Token | rem | px | Component class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius.xsmall` | 0.125rem | 2px | Badges, checkboxes, avatar labels, keyboard shortcuts |
| `radius.small` | 0.25rem | 4px | Lozenges, tags, tooltips, compact buttons |
| `radius.medium` | 0.375rem | 6px | Buttons, inputs, selects, nav items |
| `radius.large` | 0.5rem | 8px | Cards, in-page containers, dropdown menus |
| `radius.xlarge` | 0.75rem | 12px | Modals, Kanban columns, tables |
| `radius.xxlarge` | 1rem | 16px | Video players only |
| `radius.full` | pill | — | Avatars, pills, emoji reactions |
| `radius.tile` | 25% | — | Tile components only |

### Border width scale
The border foundation notes values are indicative and subject to change.

| Token | px | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `border.width` | 1px | Default hairline: input borders, card outlines, dividers, row rules |
| `border.width.selected` | 2px | Selected state (active tab/nav rail, selected card) — pair with `color.border.selected` |
| `border.width.focused` | 2px | Focus ring — pair with `color.border.focused` |

### Focus ring
- Apply with `border.width.focused` (2px) and `color.border.focused`, offset ~2px from the box; ring radius = component radius + 2px. Use the Focusable component (code) / Focus Ring (Figma). Never remove focus outlines without replacing the same contract.

### Not published
- The border foundation flags width values as "an indication only." Radius px values are quoted from `DESIGN.md`, not the border foundation page itself.
sections.iconography:
### Iconography
> Source: https://atlassian.design/components/icon/ ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

Icons ship in `@atlaskit/icon`. Glyph style: ~1.5px effective stroke, rounded outside corners, tight geometry — never mix icon packs. There are also **Object** icons (Atlassian content-type glyphs) and **Tile** (a rounded square that frames an asset).

### Sizing & color
- **Default 16×16** in product UI. For prominent contexts, place a 16px glyph inside a larger square **tile** (`background.neutral` + `icon.accent.*`) rather than scaling the glyph itself.
- Color via an `icon.*` token set as CSS `color` on a wrapper; paths use `fill="currentColor"`. Match icon role to adjacent text role (`icon.subtle` with `text.subtle`, `icon.danger` with `text.danger`).

### Accessibility
- Meaningful icons carry an accessible name; decorative icons beside a label are hidden from assistive tech.
- Never substitute Unicode arrows, emoji, or HTML-entity glyphs (`›` `→` `▶` `✓` `✕` `…` `⚠`) for real icons.

### Not published
- The `/components/icon` page is JS-rendered; a static, browsable size table isn't in the fetched HTML. `DESIGN.md` documents a single product size (16px) and the tile pattern for larger contexts — no multi-step icon size scale is published. The full SVG catalog lives in `@atlaskit/icon`.
sections.components:
### Components
> Source: https://atlassian.design/components ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

Ready-to-use React components built on **primitives + tokens**. The public inventory is grouped by need.

### Inventory (from the components index)
- **Forms & inputs:** Button, Calendar, Checkbox, Comment, Date time picker, Dropdown menu, Focus ring, Form, Radio, Range, Select, Text area, Text field, Toggle.
- **Images & icons:** Avatar, Avatar group, Icon (beta), Image (beta), Logo, Object, Tile.
- **Labels:** Badge, Date label, Lozenge, Tag, Tag group.
- **Layout & structure:** Page (caution), Page header, Panel (beta).
- **Loading:** Progress bar, Skeleton (early access), Spinner.
- **Messaging:** Banner, Empty state, Flag, Inline message, Modal dialog, Section message, Spotlight.
- **Navigation:** Breadcrumbs, Link, Menu, Navigation system, Pagination, Tabs.
- **Overlays & layering:** Blanket, Drawer, Inline dialog (caution), Popup, Tooltip.
- **Status indicators:** Progress indicator, Progress tracker.
- **Text & data display:** Code, Dynamic table, Heading (beta), Inline edit, Table (caution), Table tree, Visually hidden.

### Primitives
Box, Pressable, Anchor, Inline, Stack, Flex (beta), Grid (beta), Bleed, XCSS (caution), Responsive, Text (beta), MetricText (beta), Focusable.

### Selected behavioral recipes (from DESIGN.md)
- **Button** appearances: `default`, `primary`, `subtle`, `warning`, `danger`, `discovery`; sizes default/compact (compact only in dense surfaces). Sentence-case imperative labels; one `primary` per section; icons inherit `currentColor`.
- **IconButton**: `default`, `primary`, `discovery`, `subtle`; only when the glyph's meaning is obvious.
- **TextField**: visible label required (placeholder-as-label banned); responsive density switches at 30rem.
- **SectionMessage**: semantic role background + leading icon; body copy stays neutral `text`; icon is required.
- Sizes: Modal width tiers 400 / 600 / 800 / 968px; Tooltip 240 / 420px; Toggle 32×16 (regular) & 40×20 (large); Radio/Checkbox 16px control with 24px hit target.

### Not published
- Per-component API and token bindings aren't in the static docs — they live in component child pages, the ADS MCP server, and the `atlassian-design-system` skill. Several components are marked beta / early access / caution / deprecated.
sections.dataviz:
### Data Visualization
> Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/color/data-visualization-color ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md

ADS ships dedicated **chart color tokens** so charts meet contrast requirements. Use chart tokens for the data marks (lines, bars, slices); use border and text tokens for chart chrome (axes, labels).

### Categorical
- Eight distinct hues: `color.chart.categorical.1` … `color.chart.categorical.8`, for up to eight unrelated series.
- Use them **in numbered sequence** (series 1 → token 1) — the order guarantees each color is distinct from its neighbor across color-vision deficiencies. If display order can't be controlled (e.g. line charts), add non-color indicators.
- **Limit to 5–6 colors**; group extra categories together. Use `color.border.inverse` as a separator between adjacent chart elements.

### Single-hue tiers & semantic chart tokens
- Each hue has bold / bolder / boldest steps for value tiers, e.g. `chart.yellow.bold` `#B38600`, `chart.yellow.bolder` `#946F00`, `chart.yellow.boldest` `#7F5F01` (values from `DESIGN.md`).
- Status series use semantic chart tokens: `chart.brand` (primary metric), `chart.success`, `chart.warning`, `chart.danger`, `chart.information`, `chart.discovery`, `chart.neutral`.
- Color pickers expose ~27 chart color options (three accent shades per hue); guidance recommends avoiding yellow in pickers.

### Rule
- Must add non-color cues (patterns, shapes, labels) so charts read for colorblind users and in grayscale.

### Not published / gaps
- ADS publishes chart color tokens and usage guidance but **no charting component library** in the public docs — actual chart rendering lives in product-specific libraries. Weaker as a first-class chapter than Carbon or Spectrum.
sections.content:
### Content: Voice & Tone
> Source: https://atlassian.design/content/writing-style ; https://atlassian.design/llms-content.txt ; https://atlassian.design/content/inclusive-writing

ADS ships a complete content standard for product UI copy (also packaged as `llms-content.txt`).

### Voice & tone
- **Voice traits:** Bold · Optimistic · Practical, with a wink. Summary characteristics: clear and direct, professional yet approachable, helpful and empowering, consistent, localization-friendly.
- **Six principles:** inform to build trust · empower to inspire action · encourage people along the path · motivate by showing possibilities · satisfy by meeting expectations · delight (sparingly).
- **Tone adapts by user state:** new/learning → more prescriptive, trust-building; power users → direct, efficient; errors/frustrated → calm, solution-focused, minimal apology; success → brief celebration + next step.

### Style, grammar & punctuation (from `llms-content.txt`)
- **Sentence case** is the default for all UI text; capitalize only the first word, proper nouns, and app names.
- **Numbers:** use digits in most cases; write out a number that starts a sentence; use "to" for ranges and "of" for "out of"; comma thousands (4,500).
- **Active voice** primarily; keep sentences ~15 words; plain words over jargon.
- **Oxford (serial) comma** required. **US English** spelling.
- **Curly quotes/apostrophes** in UI (single curly quotes for UI; double for speech in long-form); punctuation inside quotes.
- **Avoid** i.e., e.g., etc., and `&` (not localization-friendly); avoid exclamation marks; contractions are encouraged.
- **Headings:** action verbs in H1s, avoid gerunds, no periods in headings/tooltips/labels; use spaced em dashes sparingly.
- **CTAs:** imperative verbs ("Save", "Delete"), never "Submit"/"OK"/"Click here". **Links:** descriptive text, never "Learn more".

### Inclusive language
- Plain language; no metaphors/idioms/jargon. Person-first language when you can't ask; specific terms for racial/ethnic groups. Gender-neutral they/them by default. Concise, consistent alt text. Descriptive links and labels; don't hide meaning behind aria-label. Thoughtful, optional identity fields; use a single "Full name" field.

### Message design
- Five message types: **information, success, warning, error, feature discovery**, each mapped to components (empty state, banner, flag, section message, inline message, modal, spotlight).
- Length: general messages ≤ 5 lines; onboarding spotlights ≤ 2 lines. Errors = reason + fix; empty states explain + give a next-step CTA.
- Appearance uses role color + icon (blue info, green success, yellow warning, red error, purple feature discovery).

### Known gaps
- Content is one of ADS's most complete public standards; no significant gaps. Some deeper terminology (go/vocab) is internal to Atlassian only.
sections.accessibility:
### Accessibility
> Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/accessibility ; https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md ; https://atlassian.design/foundations/color-new

Accessibility is baked into components (keyboard support, sensible ARIA), but teams still own end-to-end review. `DESIGN.md` states **WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor**; the color foundation cites the WCAG success criteria directly.

### Contrast
- **4.5:1** for text smaller than 24px (WCAG 1.4.3).
- **3:1** for text 24px or larger and for UI essential to understanding (WCAG 1.4.11).
- Semantic and neutral tokens already satisfy AA — don't override token text colors with off-token hex.

### Focus & keyboard
- Visible focus ring on every focusable element: `border.width.focused` (2px) + `color.border.focused`, offset with a gap; use the Focusable primitive. Never `outline: none` without an equivalent replacement.
- Every interaction reachable by keyboard alone; tab order follows visual order; no keyboard traps; `Esc` dismisses overlays.

### Principles (accessibility foundation)
- Build consistent experiences; keep language simple (target reading level ages 12–14); be inclusive; give people control (reflow, zoom, reduced motion); provide text alternatives; never rely on color alone; use semantic HTML; test broadly.
- Support 200% zoom and 320px width without loss of content or function.

### Labels & announcements
- Visible labels on form inputs (not placeholders); associate validation with fields. Accessible name on every icon-only control; decorative icons hidden. Announce dynamic changes via a `polite` live region (`assertive` only for urgent failures). One `h1` per page; never skip heading levels; use semantic landmarks.

### Known gaps / notes
- Version conflict across sources: `DESIGN.md` cites **WCAG 2.2 AA**, while the color foundation references 2.1-era criteria language. `llms-a11y.txt` was not reachable during this fetch. Some tooling (A11y Office Hours, A11y Mate, Knowledge Base) is Atlassian-internal only.
sections.dosdonts:
### Do's and Don'ts
> Source: https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md ; https://atlassian.design/components (ESLint plugin)

`DESIGN.md` ships a scan-friendly drift-pattern table; each row is a mistake to correct on sight. ADS also ships enforcement as code: `@atlaskit/eslint-plugin-design-system`, the `@atlaskit/eslint-plugin-ui-styling-standard` (UI Styling Standard), and a Stylelint plugin.

### Core do / don't
| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Padding/margin/gap on a `space.*` step | `padding: 13px` or off-rail values |
| Corner radius from `radius.*` per component class | `border-radius: 10px` not aligned to a token |
| Elevation via `shadow.overlay` / `shadow.raised` | Hand-authored `box-shadow` |
| `surface.raised` paired with `shadow.raised` | Raised surface with no paired shadow |
| `background.danger.bold` for destructive CTAs | `background.accent.red.bolder` (accent ≠ semantic) |
| Status as a **Lozenge** (semantic, bordered) | Decorative **Tag** used for status |
| Sentence case ("Create work item") | Title Case / ALL CAPS / letter-spaced eyebrows |
| Paragraphs in `text` | Body copy in `text.subtle` to "differentiate from headings" |
| SectionMessage: role background + neutral text + role icon | Blue prose on a blue information panel |
| `surface` as the page canvas, bordered cards on top | `surface.sunken` as the page background ("grey page, white cards") |
| Atlassian core icon at 16px for chevrons/checks/arrows | Unicode / emoji / entity glyphs as icons |
| Imperative CTA ("Save"), descriptive links | "Submit"/"OK"/"Click here", "Learn more" |
| Error: reason + action | "Oops, something went wrong. Please try again." |
| Empty state with a next-step CTA | "No data" / "Nothing here yet" alone |
| Atlassian Sans in product; Charlie only on marketing | Inter / Geist / SF Pro / Roboto in product |
| Focus ring per Shapes | `outline: none` with no replacement |
| `aria-label` on every icon-only control | Icon-only buttons with no accessible name |
| Borders + whitespace for depth | Glass cards, glow borders, `backdrop-filter` stacks as polish |

### Known gaps
- None material — this is a strong, published section; ESLint/Stylelint plugins make many rules machine-enforceable.
sections.agent:
### Agent Guidance
> Source: https://atlassian.design/DESIGN.md ; https://atlassian.design/llms-content.txt

ADS is delivered **agent-first**, with several machine-readable layers:
- **`llms.txt` split by topic** — content (`llms-content.txt`), accessibility, components (`llms-components.txt`), plus a full variant.
- **Portable `DESIGN.md` manifest** — a token-first standalone spec (RFC 2119 MUST/SHOULD) for generating Atlassian-style UI; a longer full-length `DESIGN.md` adds per-component API bindings, dark-anchor palettes, and prompt guidance.
- **ADS MCP server** and the **`atlassian-design-system` skill** (progressive disclosure) for token/component/lint lookup in an ADS-capable stack.
- **ESLint + Stylelint plugins** as the CI enforcement layer; **Figma Code Connect** + codemod CLI for design↔code and migrations.

### How an agent should build ADS UI
- Resolve values from **tokens**, not magic numbers; refer to tokens by name in prose/recipes, emit literal hex only in HTML/CSS output.
- Default to neutral surfaces; reserve saturation for semantic roles, accents, or charts.
- Compose on the 8px `space.*` grid; radius by component class; pair every raised/overlay surface with its shadow.
- Sentence case + imperative CTAs + descriptive links; treat all strings as translatable (allow ~30% growth).
- Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`; use `motion.duration.*` / `motion.easing.*` tokens, not hand-authored curves.

### Known gaps / not verified this run
- Exact ADS MCP tool names and the hosted MCP endpoint (`npx @atlaskit/ads-mcp`, `mcp.atlassian.com/...`) were **not re-verified from a fetched page** in this pass; `DESIGN.md` references the MCP server and skill generically. Treat specific tool signatures as unconfirmed until checked against the MCP/skill docs.
